questions.q: Why can't a distributed system rely on a single global clock?
options: Global clocks are illegal to use in production software
Every node's clock drifts at a different rate and network delivery times are unpredictable
Global clocks only work on a single physical machine's motherboard
Distributed systems never need to know what order events happened in
questions.explain: Clock drift between machines and unpredictable, out-of-order message delivery mean there is no meaningful shared "now" across a network.

questions.q: What is the key difference between synchronous and asynchronous communication?
options: Synchronous is always faster than asynchronous
Asynchronous communication never produces a response at all
A synchronous caller blocks for a response; an asynchronous caller continues immediately and the response arrives later, if ever
Synchronous communication is only possible within a single data center
questions.explain: Synchronous calls block the caller until a response returns. Asynchronous calls let the caller move on immediately, decoupling the caller's progress from the callee's speed.

questions.q: A node sends a request and receives no response. What can it conclude?
options: The target node has definitely crashed
The network is definitely down
Nothing for certain — slow, dropped message, stuck response, and crash all look identical from the outside
The request was definitely received and processed
questions.explain: Silence is ambiguous. A distributed system can only infer likely failure through timeouts and heartbeats; it can never know for certain from the absence of a response alone.

questions.q: What does Lamport's "happens-before" relation let a distributed system do?
options: Synchronize every node's wall clock exactly
Order causally related events without relying on physical clock time
Guarantee that every message arrives within a fixed time limit
Eliminate the need for asynchronous communication entirely
questions.explain: Happens-before defines a causal ordering (e.g., send before receive) that lets nodes reason about event order without comparing physical clocks, which can't be trusted to agree.

questions.q: Two events have no causal link between them under happens-before. What does that make them?
options: Synchronous
Idempotent
Concurrent — neither can be meaningfully said to have happened first
Guaranteed to have happened at the exact same physical instant
questions.explain: Events with no causal relationship are called concurrent in this model; there is no meaningful "first" between them, regardless of physical clock readings.
